issues.title: [Bug]: casting a list constructor to a readonly intersection type panics with "bad type cast"
issues.output: All three (list to int[] & readonly, mapping to readonly & map<int>, list to readonly): `error: bad type cast at main(...:4)` at runtime.
issues.edge_case_reason: Casting a list or mapping constructor to a readonly type is ordinary code.
issues.reasoning: Re-triaged because a comment added the mapping-constructor and plain `<readonly>` forms; all still reproduce on main. Spec check (clean-context subagent, reproducers only): §6.20 makes the operand's expected type the intersection with the cast type, and §6.7.1/§6.7.2 construct the value with its read-only bit on, so all three casts must succeed and print `[1,2]` / `{"x":2}` / `[1,2]`. The cast's type is the operand's contextually expected type, so the constructors must build read-only values; the BIR builds a mutable value and then casts, so the BIR is wrong -> frontend (same as the 2026-11-20 report). Related #1130, #1148, #1044; not duplicates.

issues.title: [Bug]: expression-bodied function result is not checked against the declared return type (Go interface-conversion crash)
issues.output: 1755a: prints `3` then `error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is int64, not string at main(1755a.bal:8)`; 1755b compiles with no diagnostics. BIR of g: `%0 = x; return;` with declared return string.
issues.edge_case_reason: Expression-bodied functions with a declared return type are common syntax.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec check: an expr-function-body `=> E` is short for `{ return E; }` (§7.3.3), so each marked line in 1755b must be a compile error; the observed acceptance is wrong. Missing type-check diagnostic, so the front end emits ill-typed BIR and the interpreter's Go crash is a consequence -> frontend (not runtime-crash). No duplicate found (#1122 is different).

issues.title: [Bug]: reference to a closure that reads a module variable is reported as an initialization cycle
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: invalid cycle detected for a --> 1760.bal:3:25
issues.edge_case_reason: Module variable initialised to a closure that reads another module variable referencing it; unusual cycle shape.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec check: no spec rule makes this a cycle; building the closure for `b` does not evaluate the reference to `a`, so initialising b then a works and the program should print `2` (the spec says little on module-variable ordering, so this is a judgement from first principles). A valid program is rejected by the front end -> frontend. Opposite case of #1750 (there the closure is called, so the cycle is real); `var` form hits the INTERNAL_ERROR tracked by #1327. Not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: const with an unfoldable XML-template or computed-key record default is reported as not a constant expression
issues.output: On main both programs compile and print `{}` (BIR: `ConstantLoad {}`); the record default is dropped. The reported `expression is not a constant expression` only appears at the head of the unmerged PR #925.
issues.edge_case_reason: Constant of a record type whose field default is an XML template or computed-key mapping.
issues.reasoning: The issue as written does not reproduce on main: it describes the diagnostic at the head of open PR #925 (record defaults in constant mappings), which is not merged. On main the same programs are accepted and print `{}`, silently dropping the record defaults, which is the gap #925 fixes. Spec check: printing `{}` is wrong in any case: the closed record requires the field, §6.7.2 fills defaults in a mapping constructor whose inherent type is a record, and §8.8 requires the constant's value to belong to its declared type. Expected `{"value":`x`}` / `{"m":{"k":9}}`, or an (unimplemented) compile error, never `{}`. Keep it open as a follow-up to #925 (it becomes reproducible when #925 lands); wrong/missing diagnostic -> frontend.

issues.title: [Bug]: match guards are not checked for definite assignment
issues.output: 1764a: prints `other`; 1764b: prints `other`; 1764c: prints `one` then `1`. All compile with no diagnostics.
issues.edge_case_reason: Reading a not-yet-assigned variable inside a match guard is a rare construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec check: §7 local variables and §8.7 module variables must be definitely assigned wherever referenced; the guards reference y / m before assignment, so all three programs must be rejected. Missing definite-assignment diagnostic -> frontend. Related #1638 (module-variable reads in init) and #1765; not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: uninitialized stream variable used as a method receiver compiles and crashes at runtime
issues.output: Compiles, then `error: interface conversion: values.BalValue is nil, not *values.Stream at main(1765.bal:5)`. BIR: `%2 = streamNext s` on unassigned s.
issues.edge_case_reason: Calling a method on a never-assigned stream variable is an unusual program.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces. Spec check: `s.next()` references the uninitialised local `s`, violating definite assignment; must be a compile error. Missing definite-assignment diagnostic for a stream method receiver; the runtime Go crash follows from accepting the program -> frontend. Related #1764, #1638; not a duplicate.

undetermined.reasoning: Reproduces on main e64ff12f6 (compiles, prints `2`), but validity is doubtful. The clean-context spec check (reproducer only) judged the observed behaviour CORRECT: §8.6 says a readonly class sets the object's read-only bit and intersects each field's type with readonly; it does not make fields `final`. §5.6.3's 'cannot be changed after the object has been constructed' does not cover assignments inside init, and 'assigned exactly once' applies only to fields declared `final`. The issue's claim that readonly-class fields are implicitly final follows jBallerina, not the spec text. Needs a maintainer decision: if it is accepted as a policy, label frontend (has reproducer, no internal error, edge_case false) and it is fixed by open PR #1053; otherwise close as not a bug.

Reproduces on main e64ff12f6 (LSP client against bal start-language-server, package from the issue): with `undefinedFn();` in modules/util/util.bal, publishDiagnostics for main.bal is `[]`; with it removed, main.bal gets `unused variable 'local'` and `unused variable 'n'`. Valid Type/Bug in the language server (ls/core/compile/multimodule.go dependencyErrored marks the importer phase1Errored and never compiles it). It is language-server tooling, not langlib/library/frontend/runtime; closest is frontend. Suggest frontend or a language-server label; if frontend: has reproducer, no internal error, edge_case false. Related #1485, #1567; not a duplicate.

Type/Improvement (already labelled) for CI workflows. Confirmed on main e64ff12f6: release.yml still uses actions/download-artifact@v4 and softprops/action-gh-release@v2; benchmark-pr-*-prepare.yml use upload-artifact@v4, benchmark-pr-*-comment.yml use download-artifact@v4 and github-script@v7, wasm-ci.yml uses setup-node@v4. Valid, but it is CI infrastructure, so none of langlib/library/frontend/runtime applies; suggest a CI/infra label and removing triage. No duplicate found.
